name: Oxandrolone
lead: Oxandrolone, widely known by the brand name Anavar, is an oral synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from dihydrotestosterone. It carries a 17-alpha-methyl group and a distinctive oxygen atom in its ring, which are associated with strong anabolic effect and comparatively mild androgenic effect.[1]

It has medical uses in promoting weight gain after surgery, chronic infection, severe trauma or burns, offsetting protein loss from long-term corticosteroid use, and in some paediatric conditions.[1] It is also used non-medically for lean mass and a 'cutting' physique, and some young users in looksmaxxing forums discuss it for height.[2][3]

Unlike most compounds in its class, oxandrolone has substantial randomised trial data, mainly in burns, trauma and wasting, and these indicate effects on weight and lean mass in patients. Controlled trials in healthy people for appearance were not found in the sources reviewed, and the claim that it raises adult height is not supported by the paediatric growth literature as summarised in an encyclopedic source.[1]
infobox: US Schedule III; prohibited in sport

paras: Oxandrolone is labelled to promote weight gain after extensive surgery, chronic infection or severe trauma, to counter catabolism from corticosteroids, and to relieve bone pain from osteoporosis.[1] It has been used in burn care, HIV wasting, and growth disorders including constitutional delay of growth and puberty and Turner syndrome.[1][4]

Non-medical users take it, often with testosterone, for lean mass gain and fat loss without much water retention; looksmax.org users describe it as good for cutting and as a milder add-on to a first cycle.[2][5] Some young posters ask whether it can extend growth while growth plates are open.[3][6]

Oxandrolone's 17-alpha-methyl group allows oral use but is associated with liver strain, a feature common to 17-alpha-alkylated steroids.[1] It is described as an androgen receptor agonist with tissue-selective effects that favour muscle over prostate and virilisation relative to testosterone.[1]

A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial gave oxandrolone to 62 multiple-trauma patients on enteral nutrition for up to 28 days.[7] A multicentre randomised trial studied it in AIDS-wasting myopathy,[8] and a study of anabolic effects after severe burn was published in the Annals of Surgery in 2001.[9] Reviews of burn nutrition and metabolic support discuss oxandrolone as an adjunct.[10] An encyclopedic overview cites meta-analyses in severe burns reporting reduced weight loss and faster donor-site healing, and a trial in older men reporting lean mass gain over 12 weeks.[1]

Older studies examined alcoholic hepatitis, including a Veterans Affairs cooperative trial of oral nutritional support with oxandrolone in malnourished patients[11] and a 1984 study of survival with oxandrolone and prednisolone.[12] Growth studies include randomised trials in boys with Klinefelter syndrome, one reporting an increased risk of early gonadarche[13], and trials in Turner syndrome.[4]

No trial of oxandrolone for cosmetic muscle gain or appearance in healthy people was found. Registered studies continue in injury rehabilitation, including ACL reconstruction and rotator cuff repair,[14][15] and one phase 1 study measured its bioavailability in healthy adults.[16]

Reported risks of the AAS class include liver toxicity, cardiovascular effects and hormonal disruption, and oxandrolone is stated to carry them despite its mild androgenic profile.[1] A case report described delayed rhabdomyolysis in a person using AAS.[17] Nutritional supplement analyses have also found products cross-contaminated with or faked to contain doping substances, which affects people buying unregulated products.[18]

Oxandrolone is a US Schedule III controlled substance and is banned in sport.[1] T Nation posters note that prescriptions for high doses of oxandrolone, testosterone and similar drugs sit in a legal grey area.[19]

timeline.event: First synthesised by Pappo and Jung at Searle Laboratories (per an encyclopedic overview).[1]
Introduced for medical use as Anavar.[1]
An FDA advisory review questioned the osteoporosis indication.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org oxandrolone is regarded as a mild, 'wonder' steroid and is repeatedly discussed in height-focused threads by teenagers.[3][5][6]

claims.claim: Anavar can add height or complement growth hormone in teens.
claims.believers: A 16-year-old with delayed bone age cites paediatric trials in which oxandrolone raised growth velocity and plans to use it; a 14-year-old asks about adding it to growth hormone.[3][6]
claims.experts: An encyclopedic overview says low-dose treatment raised height velocity in boys with constitutional delay but accelerated bone maturation, with adult height not differing from controls in long-term follow-up; higher doses are said to risk early growth plate closure.[1]

claims.believers: A poster says it lets users reach very low body fat, comparing it favourably to cardarine as 'more tested and safer'.[5]
claims.experts: Trials show reduced weight loss and lean mass preservation in burns and wasting.[1][7] No trials in healthy people cutting for appearance were found.

claims.claim: Anavar is a mild addition to a first test cycle.
claims.believers: Threads ask if there is any reason not to add it to a first testosterone cycle, treating it as low-risk.[2]
claims.experts: Reviews list liver and cardiovascular risks for AAS generally, and the oxandrolone overview says it carries the class's risks.[1]

card.summary: An oral steroid with real clinical trial data in burns and wasting, popular as a mild cutting drug; its height claims conflict with growth studies.
card.note: Trial benefits are in patients; teen height use contradicts the growth literature; liver and cardiac risks apply.

quick.overview:
Oxandrolone (Anavar) is an oral anabolic steroid made in the 1960s. It has been prescribed to restore weight after burns, trauma and surgery, and some people use it for a lean, dry physique.

Unusually for the category, it has randomised trials in patients showing weight and lean mass benefits. There are no controlled trials in healthy people for appearance. Teen forum posts discuss it for height, but growth studies show faster bone maturation without taller adult height, per an encyclopedic source.
quick.mechanism: It activates the androgen receptor, with relatively mild androgenic effect. The 17-alpha-methyl group allows oral use but is tied to liver strain.
quick.risks: Class risks include liver toxicity, cardiovascular effects and hormonal suppression. It is US Schedule III and banned in sport, and unregulated products can be contaminated or fake.
